name: Matar Paneer
subtitle: peas and paneer in a straightforward onion-tomato gravy, the weeknight standard
prepNotes: If the paneer is firm from the fridge, soak the cubes in hot salted water 15 minutes and drain just before adding.
Blend the onion, tomato, ginger, garlic and chilli into a smooth paste and keep it ready — this gravy comes together fast.
Frozen peas go in at the end; fresh peas need 8 minutes of simmering.

steps.text: Blend the onion, tomato, ginger, garlic and green chillies to a smooth paste with 2 tbsp water.
Heat the ghee in a kadhai, add the bay leaf and cumin seeds, and let them crackle 20 seconds.
Pour in the blended paste — stand back, it spits — and cook on medium for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: Keep going until the paste darkens to brick red and oil clearly separates at the edges. Half-cooked paste tastes raw and metallic.

steps.text: Stir in the turmeric, coriander powder and kashmiri chilli and fry 1 minute.
Add 1.5 cups water, 1 tsp salt and the sugar, and bring to a simmer.
Add the peas and simmer 8 minutes for fresh, 4 minutes for frozen, until tender.
Slide in the paneer cubes and simmer 4 minutes on low.
steps.tip: Low heat only. Boiled paneer goes tough and squeaky.

steps.text: Crush in the kasuri methi and add the garam masala.
Rest off the heat 5 minutes so the paneer takes up the gravy, then taste for salt.
Scatter the coriander and serve with roti or rice.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water. Not suitable for freezing — the paneer turns spongy.
